target_customer: Underbanked and self-employed consumers in Mexico needing small short-term loans
problem: Many Mexicans lack access to formal credit; Baubap lends small amounts via app using alternative data.
business_model: Consumer microlending (interest and fees), funded by debt facilities

founders.name: Luis Villarreal
founders.background_notes: Met Salcedo in 2016 at a media company per Crunchbase News.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring from alternative data plus lending compliance and collections; standard engineering with ML hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Repayment data compounds scoring quality; access to cheap debt is a constraint. Judgment, little sourced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of incumbents copying; Baubap says it is the leading AI lending app in Mexico.

market_need_then: Crunchbase News (Mar 2021) reports loan approval around 25%, average loan about 50 pesos, 40% self-employed borrowers, expecting 220,000+ loans in 2021, indicating unmet small-credit demand.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Baubap grew from a team of 10 and a $3M round in March 2021 to roughly 150 people by the directory snapshot, financed mostly by large debt facilities ($120M in March 2024 and a $23M facility in June 2026 per press). Growth appears debt-funded; equity rounds after 2021 were not found, so coverage is partial.
notes: Seed lead: Crunchbase News and LatamList say Grupo Alfin. Seed predates YC S21 by under 4 months. The $120M debt figure comes from several outlets in search results but crowdfundinsider and fintechfutures returned 403 on fetch, so it rests on search-result text. A $20M debt financing from Park Cities Asset Management (Nov 2022) appeared only in a search snippet and is unverified, not recorded as a round. Ongoing equity rounds may be missing.
